 Health insurance costs rise for 2027
 BY 
 Lauren Rangel
 Texas 
 PUBLISHED 3:52 PM CT Oct. 28, 2026 
 PUBLISHED 3:52 PM CDT Oct. 28, 2026 
 SHARE 
 TEXAS — It’s open enrollment season for health insurance, and next week, the Affordable Care Act (ACA) marketplace will begin enrollment, too.
 But millions of Texans may notice an increase in health insurance costs for next year.
 At the Healthy Insurance Dude offices in Hurst, near Fort Worth, it’s busy as employees take calls from people hoping to understand their 2027 health insurance options.
 “The health insurance world is nuts, but there’s a lot of options people do not realize are available,” said Perry Lunsford, CEO of the Healthy Insurance Dude. "Our job is to help people get better, more affordable health insurance.”
 According to the Kaiser Family Foundation (KFF), a health policy research center, ACA marketplace insurers are proposing a premium increase of about 15%.
 “The insurance marketplace is worse and worse every year,” said Lunsford.
 It's the second-highest proposed rate change since 2018. Last year, the median rate change nationwide was proposed at 18% but finalized at 20%.
 “We always talk to our children about compound interest,” said Lunsford. “Well, this works in the opposite way. When insurance is going up 10-15% every year, the next year it’s going up 10-20% on top of the last one.”
 This increase comes as Texas leads the country in uninsured rates.
 “Most Americans either can’t afford it or won’t afford it,” said Lunsford. 
 But Lunsford added not having health insurance can be just as costly.
 “The only thing worse than having health insurance is not,” said Lunsford. “My encouragement would be whether it’s us or another broker, find someone who genuinely understands this complicated mess and have them give you a hand."
 Affordable Care Act marketplace enrollment opens up on Nov. 1, while many Texas employers have their enrollment open now.
 Texans are also seeing big changes in who’s accepting Medicare Advantage options. For example, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas is dropping Medicare Advantage plans in the new year.
 Houston's largest health system, Memorial Hermann, is dropping the plan too. That means members will have to choose a new plan by the end of the year.
